history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - a monastic institution (math); keep-or-drop decision needed. Shanti Ashram, now the Assam Bangiya Saraswat Math, was founded by Swami Nigamananda Saraswati. It was first instituted on Akshaya Tritiya 1314 B.S. at Kumilla Durgapur, shifted to Gendaria, Dhaka in 1318 B.S., and finally established on an 80-bigha plot at Kumarveti Chapri village, Kokilamukh (near Jorhat), where Nigamananda installed the Brahma asana on 7th Baisakh 1319 B.S. and named it Shanti Ashram; it has been called Assam Bangiya Saraswat Math since 1325 B.S. His three missions: propagate Sanatana Dharma, spread true education, and serve everyone as god incarnate. The math has about 50 branch Saraswat ashrams in India and abroad and publishes the Saraswat Granthabali. CSV town 'Jorhat' is approximate: the actual site is Kokilamukh, about 7 km from Jorhat town. Wikipedia coordinates (26.830650, 94.178800) are corroborated by geocoding (26.83084, 94.17819).

name: Shanti Ashram
town_description: Jorhat is a major city of Upper Assam, the cultural heart of the Neo-Vaishnavite tradition and the historic tea capital, home to the Tocklai Tea Research Institute. It is the main gateway to Majuli, the river island of the satras, via the Nimati Ghat ferry.
tradition: Hindu monastic (Saraswata/Dashanami lineage under Sringeri tradition)

travel.airport: Jorhat Airport (JRH), about 7 km away; the math is at Kokilamukh, about 7 km west of Jorhat town
travel.railway: Jorhat Town railway station, about 8 km away
travel.road: Connected by road from Jorhat town via Kokilamukh; Jorhat lies on NH-27/NH-37 links to Guwahati and Dibrugarh

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Akshaya Tritiya (April/May) is the main annual celebration
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented; contact the math before visiting
